title: What an Airline Schedule Move Confers on an Air Ticket Fare Brands Booking
content:
An airline schedule move at or beyond the threshold of the Air Ticket Fare Brands brand held gives the traveller a right to be rebooked at no charge onto any flight the airline will accept, or to be refunded in full to the original form of payment whatever the brand's ordinary refund form.

## 1. Below the threshold

A move smaller than the brand's threshold gives no right. A traveller who still wants to move pays the brand's disruption rebooking fee, and a traveller who still wants to cancel is treated as a voluntary cancellation.

| The largest single move on one segment | What the traveller acquires |
| --- | --- |
| at or beyond the brand's threshold | rebooking at no charge onto any flight the airline will accept, or a refund in full to the original form of payment |
| below the brand's threshold, and the traveller wishes to move | no right; the brand's disruption rebooking fee is payable |
| below the brand's threshold, and the traveller wishes to cancel | no right; treated as a voluntary cancellation |

## 2. How several notices are read

Several notices on the same booking are not added together; the largest single move on any one segment decides the right, and a notice later withdrawn by the airline is disregarded.

An airline cancellation of the segment is always treated as a move beyond the threshold, whatever its recorded minutes.

## 3. Overnight stays

Where the rebooking obliges the traveller to stay overnight, the brand's overnight allowance is reimbursed per traveller per night against a receipt, and a brand with no allowance reimburses nothing.

## 4. Repeated moves

A booking that has received more than 3 notices in the last ninety days is passed to the disruption desk rather than rebooked again, because repeated moves indicate the schedule itself is unstable.

## 5. Hypothetical readings

On a brand whose threshold is 120 minutes, a booking carrying two notices of 70 and 90 minutes acquires no right: the two are not added, and the largest single move, 90 minutes, falls below the threshold. Had one of the two been an airline cancellation of the segment, the right would stand whatever minutes that notice recorded.

A booking carrying 3 notices in the last ninety days is not yet past the count in section 4, since that clause turns on more than 3; a fourth notice in the same ninety days passes it, and the booking goes to the disruption desk.
